title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
summary: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite group, we obtain new double affine versions of the quantum wreath Hecke algebras, and in particular of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the centre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.

title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
summary: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

title: Quantum Color Newton Rings
summary: We study integral Newton rings attached to symmetric quantum colors. We show that their boundary values at a deleted node are exactly the elements of Habiro's cyclotomic completion, and we describe their quantum neighborhoods at $q=1$ uniformly in the rank. The symmetric-color $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ invariants of a knot are the values of an element of such a ring. In its expansion at $q=1$, the coefficient of $(q-1)^m$ has denominator dividing the $(n-1+2m)$th power of the Alexander polynomial, with integral numerator, and this exponent is sharp. For $5_2$ and $6_1$ at $q=i$, the period matrices of the rank-two coefficient recurrences have spectral modules of exact order three in the Picard group of an affine elliptic curve.

title: Operator Algebraic Quantum Hypergroups
summary: We develop a theory of operator algebraic quantum hypergroups and their representations, formulated using a special case of the algebraic quantum hypergroup framework of van Daele and Delvaux. As part of the axioms, every operator algebraic quantum hypergroup admits a dual object of the same type. We prove that a certain universal completion in the compact case satisfies the axioms of an earlier notion of a compact quantum hypergroup in the sense of the second author and Chapovsky. As part of this theory, we discuss their (co)amenability properties. We consider examples induced by conditional expectations of algebraic quantum groups satisfying certain properties, which include quantum hypergroups corresponding to double cosets and automorphisms of quantum groups, and quantum hypergroups induced by representation categories of Kac type compact quantum groups.

title: Fiber product of condensable algebras and critical points of boundary phase transitions
summary: In this work, we propose a mathematical description of the critical point of boundary phase transitions in 2+1D topological orders. Given two boundary phases, $\mathcal{C}_A$ and $\mathcal{C}_B$, with corresponding Lagrangian algebras $A$ and $B$ in a 2+1D topological order $\mathcal{C}$, respectively, we propose that the critical point of the phase transition between these two phases, if it exists, corresponds to $D = A \times_{M} B$, which is the fiber product of $A$ and $B$ over $A$-$B$-algebra $M$. We prove that $D$ is also a condensable algebra. Additionally, we present an alternative classification of condensable algebras in $Z(Vec_G^ω)$ and reveal splitting phenomenon that arises during the condensation of certain algebras. We also perform explicit computations for the condensable algebras within several examples of $Z(Vec_G^ω)$, covering both Abelian and non-Abelian groups $G$.

title: On connection between associators and 6j-symbols
summary: We propose a new formula relating the rationalized Drinfeld associators obtained from the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation to the quantum $6j$-symbols of the algebra $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})$: $ U_{q} = U \cdot Φ^{KZ}_{\mathbb{Q}} $. We prove this relation in the case of the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental and the first symmetric representation. We also check it perturbatively for the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ algebra for representations $[2]\otimes [1] \otimes [1]$, $[2]\otimes [2] \otimes [1]$, the non-trivial cases with multiplicities --- $[2,1]^{\otimes 3}$, $[2,2]^{\otimes 3}$, and in the case of the $\mathfrak{so}_5$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental representation.

title: Integral forms for Yangians of classical type
comment: v1 28 pages, comments welcome!; v2 43 pages, classified finite dimensional simple modules of small and restricted Yangians by restricted Drinfeld polynomials; revised the introduction and exposition
summary: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a simple Lie algebra of classical type. We construct a $\mathbb Z[1/2]$-integral form of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak g)$ generated by divided powers of the positive and negative Drinfeld generators, and establish its triangular decomposition and PBW basis. Under the loop filtration, its associated graded algebra is the current algebra part of Garland's integral form. As applications, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>3$, we identify the small Yangian with the restricted Yangian and classify their finite dimensional simple modules in terms of restricted Drinfeld polynomials.

title: A Functorial Theory of Defects in Abelian Chern-Simons Theory
summary: Recent work has constructed Abelian Chern-Simons theories as categorical TQFTs, allowing us to naturally incorporate categorical defects and construct defect extensions of Abelian Chern-Simons TQFTs. We first identify the Turaev-Viro realizations of Abelian Chern-Simons theory in the center and doubled pointed modular cases, clarifying the distinction between single bulk realizations and canonical doubled ones. Then we obtain Turaev-Viro partition functions in terms of Reidemeister-torsion densities. Alternatively, the Alterfold construction supplies the associated topological boundaries, domain walls, and condensation sectors, establishing an explicit Alterfold/Chern-Simons dictionary. We show that the finite quadratic module is the invariant controlling the bulk theory, its topological symmetries, orientation-reversal invariance, and defects. We further show that multicomponent Abelian BF theory arises as the extended TQFT of an off-diagonal Abelian Chern-Simons theory, placing it naturally within the same extended framework. Finally, we demonstrate that recently proposed Abelian Chern-Simons dualities do not define a genuine TQFT duality. These results provide a concrete model for defects in Abelian topological orders and suggest a route toward the non-Abelian case.

title: Coordinates for ${\rm SL}_3$-web basis elements in closed surfaces
comment: 30 pages. Accepted version, to appear in Advances in Mathematics
summary: The ${\rm SL}_3$-skein algebra of a closed surface $Σ_g$ is a quantization of the ${\rm SL}_3$ character variety of $Σ_g$, where $g$ denotes the genus of the surface. This algebra admits a basis consisting of non-elliptic web diagrams in $Σ_g$ after Sikora--Westbury. In this paper, we introduce explicit ${\rm SL}_3$ version of Dehn--Thurston coordinates for non-elliptic web diagrams on $Σ_g$, yielding a parametrization by a submonoid of $\mathbb Z^{d}$. The idea is to tropicalize the Fenchel--Nielsen coordinates for the ${\rm SL}_3$-Hitchin component. Here $d = 16g - 16$ for $g \ge 2$ and $d = 4$ in the torus case $g = 1$, coinciding with the dimension of the corresponding character variety.

title: Seifert cobordisms and the Chen-Yang volume conjecture
comment: Minor revisions following referee suggestions. To appear in Journal of London Math. Society
summary: We study the large $r$ asymptotic behavior of the Turaev-Viro invariants $TV_r(M; e^{\frac{2πi}{r}})$ of 3-manifolds with toroidal boundary, under the operation of gluing a Seifert-fibered 3-manifold along a component of $\partial M$. We show that the Turaev-Viro invariants volume conjecture is closed under this operation. As an application we prove the volume conjecture for all Seifert fibered 3-manifolds with boundary and for large classes of graph 3-manifolds.

title: Approximation of graded bialgebras
comment: V3: We have revised Section 2.2, clarified an argument in the proof of Proposition 3.9 in V2, and corrected the proof of Theorem 3.11 in V2
summary: Motivated by an equivalence of categories established by Kapranov and Schechtman, we introduce, for each non-negative integer d, the category of connected bialgebras modulo d+1. We show that these categories fit into an inverse system of categories whose inverse limit category is equivalent to the category of connected bialgebras. In addition, we extend the notion of approximation of connected bialgebras to those that are not necessarily generated in degree 1 and show that, for connected bialgebras in the category of Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a Hopf algebra, approximation is compatible with cocycle twisting.

title: Computing the center of a fusion category
comment: Final version to appear in Comm. Math. Phys. (thanks to the referees for several helpful comments)
summary: We present an algorithm for explicitly computing the categorical (Drinfeld) center of a pivotal fusion category. Our approach is based on decomposing the images of simple objects under the induction functor from the category to its center. We have implemented this algorithm in a general-purpose software framework TensorCategories for tensor categories that we develop within the open-source computer algebra system OSCAR. We compute explicit models for the centers in form of the tuples $(X,γ)$ where $X$ is an object and $γ$ is a half-braiding. From these models we can compute the $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols. Using the data from the AnyonWiki, we were able to compute the center together with its $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols for all the 279 multiplicity-free fusion categories up to rank 5, and furthermore some chosen examples of rank 6, including the Haagerup subfactor (presented in a separate paper). Some of these centers yield new high-rank and not multiplicity-free examples of modular categories, e.g. rank 21 and multiplicity 2.
